speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been present and if you have noticed any fever or chills? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, C-Reactive_Protein, ESR.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your blood work and inflammatory markers are normal, the ulcer is less likely to be an acute bacterial infection. Does the wound have a "punched-out" appearance with a distinct border, and has this lesion been present for several months or longer?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Crohn's Cutis Levdii (cutaneous Crohn's disease).

The one-month history, history of Crohn's disease treated with corticosteroids, and the specific progression from a red spot following a minor trauma (ant bite) are classic for this condition. The normal inflammatory markers further support this over an acute bacterial infection.
